The ending feels entirely natural and earned because it represents the culmination of Nora's character arc and the central conflict of the story—her "absorption" and restructuring by her wealthy mother-in-law. Throughout the piece, the narrative builds toward whether Nora will resist Miss Emily's transactional worldview or align with it. In the final lines, the story brings back key motifs established earlier: Nora consciously corrects her working-class physical tic (un-tucking her thumb, as Miss Emily instructed in the beginning), dismisses her old cheap dress, fixes her husband's frayed collar, and seamlessly delivers the exact piece of manipulative advice Miss Emily fed her at lunch. It is the exact moment the entire piece was leading toward, providing a chillingly complete resolution to the story's themes of class, service, and assimilation.
